# Moovicut

> Free, local-first storyboard and shot list. No account and no video rendering.

Prompts work with Grok Imagine, Google, or any other AI image or video model. Moovicut does not render video. The website UI is in English and Portuguese (`?lang=`, stored as `moovicut.language`). In the studio, fixed prompt lines follow that language. The typed idea, names, places, and actions stay as written. API field `promptLanguage` (alias `prompt_language`) is optional and defaults to `en`, so an existing client still gets the English prompt. JSON field names stay English. Free-prose detection reads English and Portuguese. Detection stays rule-based. Nothing is sent to an external AI. It does not call a model. Places come from a static library (`app/data/place-lexicon.json`, licence CC BY-SA 4.0 for the compilation). A sure place can name the setting when it appears. An ambiguous word counts only in a locative. A scene keeps its place until a new locative sentence, a beat whose subject names a new place, or a movement such as crosses, wades into, caminha até, or vai para replaces it. Sea and beach stay different places. A watch is never a place. A sentence where someone enters also replaces the place. The place is the first noun after that preposition, kept even when it is not in the library, and the shot is flagged. A passing mention does not. An adjective, a garment, and a possessive are never the place. An uncertain reading is not used to fill names. Free prose is split on place and time cues unless `splitScenes` is false. The current firm place wins, and a sentence with no listed verb is kept. An article inside a venue name is not a place cue. Each cut has a cue and a reason. A character with no look is a warning, not a rejection.

- [Product guide](product.md): local planning, storage, and output.
- [FAQ](faq.md): models, local work, export, and storage.
- [Full agent guide](llms-full.txt): document contract, browser automation, and CLI examples.
- [Output map](agents.md): which request body for which film — start there.
- [Site index](index.md): routes and local workflow. The studio is `/studio`.
- [Agents](agents.md): `/mcp`, `GET /openapi.json`, `POST /api/v1/storyboard`, `/agents`, and `GET /api/v1/manifest` — the self-certified contract: every success payload carries a re-computable `sha256`.
- [README](README.md): the project README, also at `/readme`. Raw Markdown is `/README.md`.
- [Skill](SKILL.md): the agent skill, also at `/skill`. Raw Markdown is `/SKILL.md`.
- [Credits](credits): place-library sources and the CC BY-SA 4.0 compilation licence.

The default video prompt is short (`prompt_style` `short` or `detailed`): the framing term in the prompt language, the character name, and the action, then each person’s full lock line, the full place, one light, and the style with a locked-off camera unless a movement was set. The order is the same in every language. No lens unless one was set. Under about 700 characters. Fitting never shortens the action or the lock line. A character packet exports the lock, the sheet, and the prompts. Moovicut does not call an image or video API. `detailed` keeps the full film sheet in every shot. The sheet itself stays on the board and in `shotboard.compact.v1`. A hand-edited prompt is kept when the prompt style changes. Description sentences fill the character sheet and are not shots. A sentence that only sets the place, the time, or a person's appearance is not a shot either. A lock line keeps the age, the full appearance phrase, and a carried item, and matching is on word boundaries. A Portuguese role keeps the gender written in the text. Portuguese night cues (`à noite`, `meia-noite`, `madrugada`, `ao anoitecer`, `ao luar`) set night light from that sentence until the next time cue. `Ao entardecer`, `crepúsculo`, and `ao pôr do sol` set dusk. At midday, in the afternoon, and à tarde set midday or afternoon and replace an earlier dawn. A compound place keeps the full phrase. Leaving an interior returns to the previous outdoor place. Giving an item back, or deixa cair or perde, moves the item. A lock line is nouns. Os dois names both characters when the cast is two, and a avó names the person introduced as the grandmother. A later veste, põe, tira, or despe versions the outfit. An explicit morning or dawn cue replaces that night. A manner adverb, an idiom, and a trailing `com` tool phrase are not places. A time-jump locative adopts the new place. A description that sets the time keeps its place. Lock lines repeat age, hair, outfit, item, and role on every shot. Do not shorten a long story: `invalid_plan` says to resubmit the full text as prose, and `GET /api/v1/storyboard` points to `POST`. A language, a body part, a room surface, an object, and a clothing phrase are never places, and a rejected candidate is not carried. A movement into a new location adopts the noun phrase even when it is not in the lexicon. One action beat is one shot: count the actions, never merge or drop one, send the whole scenario in one request, list only the people in that shot, set `time` (`dawn`, `morning`, `midday`, `afternoon`, `dusk`, `evening`, `night`) when the story names the time of day, and split a story over 40 shots into parts. `evening`, `morning`, `afternoon`, and `midday` in `light` are stored as `time`. A warning with `action` `none` is done. Any re-post must resend every scene. A scenario that packs many actions into few shots is HTTP 400 `invalid_plan`. A later first name aliases the full name. A story with no named place still plans, with that place marked uncertain. Time of day applies from the sentence that states it, forward only. A story longer than 40 shots is split into parts of at most 40 shots. The same character sheet and place sheet are reused across parts. The default board is 5 scenes × 3 seconds (15s). Pass `shots`, `duration`, or a `scenes` array for a custom scene-by-scene board. Humans can do the same with Step-by-step mode in `/studio`. Scenario mode accepts a `scenario` object or text. When the story names people, send character sheets and do not send `input: "prose"`. `format` `agent` on prose returns HTTP 200 with `sheets_missing` and `sheets` to resubmit. `input: "prose"` remains for a premise that names nobody. A plain premise shaped as `Name, trait, trait` keeps those people, splits look and outfit, and uses the real action sentences as shots. Prose that cannot be planned is HTTP 400 and the message lists each missing piece. A premise that names people or several actions, and that cannot be planned into those shots, is HTTP 400 `invalid_plan`, not a template board. Characters, places, and scenes sent at the top level, instead of inside `scenario`, are HTTP 400 `misplaced_scenario_fields`. The message names each field and shows a short example. That error outranks `invalid_premise` when the premise is missing. Scene `what` and `who` count toward `invalid_plan`. Age and role stay in the character lock line. A constraint such as "without touching", "不接触", or "sem se tocar" stays in the short prompt and the detailed prompt. A shot size already written in the action is used once, and the response adds a `shot_size_in_action` warning. The message names every dropped person and quotes every dropped action, each one ending in a period (`This action was not planned: "Maya hands Rui a letter on the quay".`). Send a scenario. `who` and `w` accept a string or a list of names. A wrong shape says that a string or a list of names is expected. `format` `agent` warns with `empty_characters` or `empty_places` when that list is empty, and with `empty_who` or `empty_where` on a scenario shot. A Chinese short prompt names the subject, then the place with 在, then the action, with no full stop between the name and the verb. A body part, a garment, or a similar noun is never a place. A names-only scenario is 400 with each problem in `message`. `splitActions: false` keeps a multi-action line in one shot; otherwise the API splits it. `format: "agent"` includes `warnings` when a shot looks risky. The same verb is not counted twice, so `He walks away` is not too many actions. `mode` `ad` turns a product and a benefit into hook, hero, proof, and pack shot, with the product locked on the film sheet. `mode` `series` plans 3 to 8 vertical episodes on one film sheet. `mode` `explainer` turns a numbered list into one action per shot and snaps each duration to the selected model profile. Presets `anime` (`manga` is an alias), `cinema`, and `documentary` lock style into every generated shot, including a plain premise. An unknown family is 400. A shot marked `promptEdited`, including a prompt you send on a scene or on a posted `shotboard.compact.v1` board, is kept unless `overwritePrompt` is true. `mode` `series` is 3 to 8 episodes, three shots each, so the default of 3 episodes is 9 shots. `regenerateShot` plus `project` rebuilds one shot. `warnings` is included only when a shot looks risky, and it never blocks the board. Every mode shares one film sheet. `format: "agent"` returns `shotboard.compact.v1`. Minified JSON, with no extra whitespace, is the token-efficient way to send that compact document. A scenario may omit `premise`; the idea line is then the character and place names, not the first scene’s action. A scene whose only names are public figures, brands, or trademarks returns the neutral risk note and does not add missing-character or missing-place lines. A personal library of characters, places, and styles stays in the browser and can be exported. `model` accepts grok, google, sora, chatgpt, midjourney, hailuo, seedance, pika, kling, runway, luma, wan, or generic. Veo clips are 4, 6, or 8 seconds in 16:9 or 9:16. Unverified limits are marked in `app/utils/model-profiles.js`. Sources for the profiles added on 2026-11-16 are in `docs/model-profiles.md`.

Canonical schema: `shotboard.v1`. Canonical browser API: `window.Shotboard` (`window.Moovicut` is the same object). CLI: `node cli/moovicut.mjs` (`shotboard` is the same command). Remote API: `POST /api/v1/storyboard`. MCP: `POST /mcp`. A2A: `POST /a2a` (`message/send`, card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`). Discovery: `/.well-known/mcp.json`. No API key and no stored premises.
